title: Familiar Words, Unfamiliar Minds: Conventionalization without Calibration in the Vocabulary of Mind
abstract: arXiv:2611.34179v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speakers describe new technologies by stretching old words, letting experience of the new referents sort out which inferences carry over. I argue that stretching the vocabulary of mind to language models pulls apart two processes that theories of metaphor and linguistic change tend to conflate: conventionalization, whereby a stretched word ceases to be marked as such, and calibration, whereby the inferences it invites are fitted to what its new referents bear out. As a gene variant can reach fixation without being an adaptation, a word can become conventional without being calibrated. A corpus study of "hallucinate" in 8,568 abstracts and 31,866 forum comments shows conventionalization running most of its course within three years. Calibration need not keep pace: these models are organized so unlike human minds that it is hard to tell when mental words apply and what they imply. translated_title: 熟悉的词语，陌生的心智：心智词汇中的无校准惯例化
translated_abstract: 说话者通过延伸旧词来描述新技术，让对新指称对象的经验来厘清哪些推断可以延续。我认为，将心智词汇延伸至语言模型，会分离出隐喻理论与语言演变理论常常混为一谈的两个过程：惯例化——即被延伸的词不再被标记为特殊用法；以及校准——即该词所引发的推断被调整以匹配其新指称对象所能证实的内容。正如一个基因变异可以在并非适应性演化的情况下达到固定，一个词也可以在未经校准的情况下成为惯例用法。一项针对8,568篇摘要和31,866条论坛评论中“幻觉”一词的语料库研究显示，惯例化在三年内基本完成。然而校准未必与之同步：这些模型的组织方式与人类心智迥然不同，以至于很难判断心智词汇何时适用、又意味着什么。即使是有依据的归因也可能造成误导：机制分析……
tldr: 该论文区分了将心智词汇延伸至语言模型时的两个独立过程——“惯例化”与“校准”，并通过对“幻觉”一词的语料库研究表明，词汇可在三年内完成惯例化，但由于语言模型与人类心智的组织方式根本不同，其推断含义的校准未必同步，甚至有依据的心智归因也可能误导。
en_tdlr: The paper distinguishes conventionalization from calibration when the vocabulary of mind is stretched to language models, showing via a corpus study of "hallucinate" that a word can become conventional within three years without its inferences being calibrated, since these models are organized so unlike human minds that even warranted mental attributions can mislead.
